extracted.intended_audience: news editors, wire-service journalists, and general newspaper readers
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and editing frontline/foreign-war dispatches for newspapers and radio using wire services and military communiques; balancing timeliness, verification, operational security, and sensitivity to morale. Includes use of photographs, refugee testimony, and official statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of wire services and communiques
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper and the radio both subscribe to the Associated Press, United Press, and International News Service; communiques and dispatches from these agencies are used as source material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in text: on some occasions agency copy has been 'too "hot"' and a last-minute decision was made to carry only the text of communiques. Use wire copy but be prepared to edit or delay material judged inappropriate or unverified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint regarding graphic frontline despair
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither has used any stories reflecting the despair and shock of frontline American troops after their first contact with the enemy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army officers watch Stars and Stripes and the Armed Forces Radio 'for their effect on troop morale.' Presumably withhold certain ugliness or graphic details—especially those that might affect young soldiers or public morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph selection and impactful captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of full front-page layouts of pictures (e.g., showing surrendered or killed soldiers) accompanied by strong captions (example caption: 'WITHOUT A CHANCE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers range from showing loneliness of outposts to vivid portrayals of heat and dirt; choose images that convey story while weighing sensitivity and morale implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting identities of vulnerable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Refugees' names are withheld to prevent harm to relatives left behind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing testimony from displaced persons or others at risk, withhold identifying details to protect subjects and their families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling confidential material and source caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Tokyo sent a note 'confidential and not for publication'; Moore telephoned a brief dispatch and remarked he had to be 'very careful' about what he said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat confidential tips and off-the-record comments cautiously; do not publish material explicitly labeled 'not for publication' and verify before using. Press for material that is 'publishable' while respecting source restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge uncertainty and conflicting reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements such as 'first reports here are meager', 'the sequence of other events was not clear', and conflicting newspaper accounts about Syngman Rhee illustrate uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag meager or contradictory information, attribute accounts, and avoid definitive assertions until corroborated; report ambiguities transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official communiques, timestamps, and attributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Military communiques (e.g., 'a communique issued by General MacArthur's headquarters at 1310 Japan daylight time...') are used and dated/attributed precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include times, locations, and clear attribution to official sources when reporting military movements and actions to support verifiability and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withhold operationally sensitive details
rubrics_metrics.description: References to being 'very careful' and to material being 'too hot' imply withholding facts that could affect troop morale or security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish operational details that could endanger troops, reveal vulnerabilities, or compromise military operations; coordinate with official guidance when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eyewitness and soldier quotes with contextual framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct quotes from soldiers and pilots (e.g., 'We couldn't find that blasted gun,' 'we'll show these gooks a fight') are used to convey immediacy and perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish vivid firsthand remarks to convey atmosphere, but provide context, avoid gratuitous language, and consider editorial standards for taste and potential offense.
